quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report; continuing operations): revenue JPY 3,502.9 billion (-1.3% YoY), operating profit JPY 348.3 billion (+31.4%), adjusted operating profit JPY 390.5 billion (+27.1%; up in every segment) with an adjusted operating margin of 11.2% (8.7% a year earlier), after excluding JPY 42.2 billion of one-time losses mainly from European and domestic hardware restructuring. Profit attributable to owners of the parent JPY 449.4 billion (+104.5%), including a JPY 40.0 billion gain on the sale of Fujitsu General shares (equity-method income) and a JPY 141.5 billion gain on the sale of Shinko Electric shares (discontinued operations); adjusted net profit JPY 298.2 billion (+23.8%), adjusted EPS JPY 169.1 (JPY 132.6). Management states revenue rose in Service Solutions on higher Uvance and modernization orders, mainly in Japan, but fell company-wide on the reaction to large public-sector hardware deals a year earlier and the end of OS-upgrade PC demand; both net profit and adjusted operating profit were record highs. No single customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue JPY 3,502.9 billion (-1.3%); adjusted operating profit JPY 390.5 billion (+27.1%), margin 11.2%

quarterly_data.signal: Service Solutions, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): revenue JPY 2,346.9 billion (+4.5%), adjusted operating profit JPY 361.4 billion (+24.7%), margin 15.4% (12.9%); the profit gain came from higher revenue (+JPY 41.0 billion, led by Japan), margin improvement (+JPY 43.7 billion, including standardization / automation and generative AI in development) and higher growth investment (-JPY 13.2 billion); gross margin 38.7%, up 2 points again. Global Solutions revenue JPY 540.6 billion (+5.7%), adjusted operating profit JPY 33.3 billion (6.2%); Regions (Japan) JPY 1,366.8 billion (+4.3%), adjusted operating profit JPY 293.9 billion (21.5%); Regions (International) JPY 575.2 billion (-2.5%), adjusted operating profit JPY 34.1 billion (5.9%) - Europe JPY 400.9 billion (+2.7%, operating margin 6.6%), Americas JPY 52.0 billion (-8.7%), Asia Pacific JPY 90.9 billion (-11.7%), East Asia JPY 28.8 billion (-23.8%). Uvance revenue JPY 709.3 billion (+47%), above the JPY 700.0 billion target, with Vertical up 69% (led by data and AI) and more than 40% of Uvance revenue; Uvance rose to 30% of Service Solutions revenue (21%). Modernization revenue JPY 392.1 billion (+32%), well above the JPY 330.0 billion target (JPY 249.7 billion, +24%, excluding the overlap with Uvance), 11% of Service Solutions. Uvance and modernization together grew from JPY 281.5 billion in the year to March 2023 to JPY 959.0 billion in the year to March 2026, 41% of Service Solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: Service Solutions revenue JPY 2,346.9 billion (+4.5%), adjusted operating profit JPY 361.4 billion (15.4%); Uvance revenue JPY 709.3 billion (+47%)

quarterly_data.signal: Hardware Solutions, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): revenue JPY 1,009.8 billion (-9.8%), adjusted operating profit JPY 67.0 billion (+9.3%), margin 6.6% (5.5%). System Products (servers, storage) revenue JPY 816.2 billion (-13.0%) on the reaction to large public-sector deals a year earlier, reduced sales of externally purchased products and the scaling back of small low-margin businesses in Asia; the integrated development-manufacturing-sales structure of Fsas Technologies (the server / storage business carved out in April 2024) improved profitability. Network Products revenue JPY 193.6 billion (+6.6%) on base-station equipment deliveries brought forward, with profit up as 1FINITY (the photonics-system and mobile-system network products business spun off on July 1, 2025, aiming among other things to expand into the AI data center market) improved efficiency. Ubiquitous Solutions (PCs) revenue JPY 229.8 billion (-8.7%), adjusted operating profit JPY 38.8 billion (16.9%) after Windows 10 end-of-support demand ran its course, helped by a shift to higher-value products. Corporate / eliminations adjusted operating loss JPY 76.7 billion, roughly flat, for advanced research in AI, quantum computers and next-generation CPUs and the One Fujitsu program.
quarterly_data.figure: Hardware Solutions revenue JPY 1,009.8 billion (-9.8%), adjusted operating profit JPY 67.0 billion (6.6%); System Products JPY 816.2 billion (-13.0%); Network Products JPY 193.6 billion (+6.6%)

quarterly_data.signal: Orders, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): Service Solutions orders in Japan were 102% of the prior year, 108% excluding large multi-year deals of JPY 2.5 billion or more each, with strong DX demand all year - Enterprise roughly flat (106% excluding large deals), Finance 94% (105%), Public and Healthcare 105% (108%), Mission Critical 102% (113%, national security especially strong). Japan Service Solutions order backlog at year-end JPY 1,127.0 billion (107% of the prior year-end), of which JPY 1,033.0 billion is scheduled for revenue in the year to March 2027 (110%). Overseas orders: Europe roughly flat for the year; Americas 82% and Asia Pacific 93% of the prior year on the reaction to large public-sector deals. Uvance orders JPY 727.5 billion (+33%); modernization orders JPY 399.2 billion (+4%), above the prior year's level that included many large multi-year deals.
quarterly_data.figure: Japan Service Solutions orders 102% of prior year (108% excluding large deals); Japan order backlog 107% of prior year-end; Uvance orders JPY 727.5 billion (+33%)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook and strategy (annual securities report): from the year to March 2027 Fujitsu replaces three-year plans with a ten-year 'Vision 2035' set with yearly targets, centred on Technology-driven value creation (AI, computing) and support for AI-driven management, and on three new-business areas - Sovereign Platform (more energy-efficient, secure computing power), Physical AI and Intelligent Society. For the year to March 2027 it plans Japan Service Solutions revenue of JPY 1,960.0 billion (111% of the prior year), with the order backlog covering 53% of the plan (about the usual level); it will keep growing Uvance and modernization, shift from region-based to industry-based management, again target a 2-point gross margin improvement, and further step up investment in advanced research centred on the Takane LLM and Kozuchi AI platform, a superconducting quantum computer of more than 10,000 qubits and the next-generation FUJITSU-MONAKA processor. Management states adjusted operating profit set a record for a fourth straight year, with company adjusted operating margin rising from 6.6% in the year to March 2021 to 11.2% in the year to March 2026 and Service Solutions from 6.0% to 15.4%.
quarterly_data.figure: Japan Service Solutions revenue plan JPY 1,960.0 billion (111%); backlog coverage 53%

quarterly_data.signal: Next-generation CPU (annual securities report): Fujitsu is developing the next-generation processor FUJITSU-MONAKA with strategic partners; in October 2025 it announced an expanded strategic collaboration with NVIDIA to build AI infrastructure combining domain-specific AI agents running on a computing platform carrying Fujitsu CPUs and NVIDIA GPUs, and development is under way. Fujitsu received an order from RIKEN for the basic design of the next flagship system after the Fugaku supercomputer (development code name 'FugakuNEXT'), which will combine advanced technologies applied in FUJITSU-MONAKA, built on leading-edge 2-nanometer technology, and its successor 'FUJITSU-MONAKA-X' (tentative name). Fujitsu also announced 'Fujitsu Kozuchi Physical AI 1.0', developed in collaboration with NVIDIA, to link Physical AI and AI agents.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: partner (strategic collaboration: Fujitsu CPUs with NVIDIA GPUs)

quarterly_data.signal: R&D and quantum (annual securities report): group R&D expenses JPY 137.3 billion for the year to March 2026 - Service Solutions JPY 26.4 billion, Hardware Solutions JPY 58.6 billion, corporate / eliminations JPY 52.2 billion. In April 2025, in joint research with RIKEN, Fujitsu announced a 256-qubit superconducting quantum computer (company: among the world's largest), offered from the April-June 2025 quarter; a dedicated quantum computer facility at Fujitsu Technology Park (Kawasaki) was completed in September 2025, where a 1,024-qubit-class machine (company: the world's largest scale) is to be developed and installed in FY2027 (the year to March 2027); the target is a superconducting quantum computer of more than 10,000 physical qubits in FY2031 (the year to March 2031). Other results: an AI-Driven Software Development Platform using the Takane LLM, and a gallium nitride (GaN) HEMT power-amplifier technology achieving 74.3% power-conversion efficiency at 8 GHz (company: world's highest).
quarterly_data.figure: R&D JPY 137.3 billion (Hardware Solutions JPY 58.6 billion); 1,024-qubit-class machine planned in FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Capital expenditure (annual securities report): JPY 50.3 billion in the year to March 2026 (-2.3%), of which Service Solutions JPY 17.2 billion, mainly service-business facilities including data center facilities.
